assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED is the architectural basis of essentially all superconducting quantum processors: strong coupling of an artificial atom to a single microwave photon, dispersive readout and the transmon-resonator toolkit. It is original, clear and has reshaped both quantum optics and quantum computing. I judge it from close subject-matter familiarity, which I should disclose.
assessment.attribution: The 2004 theory (Blais, Huang, Wallraff, Girvin, Schoelkopf) and the Yale experiments are the decisive core; Schoelkopf (experiment and transmon-era engineering), Girvin (theory and leadership) and Blais (theory) form a coherent trio. Wallraff, Huang, Majer and Koch are not available in the supplied credit and a real allocation would be contested.
assessment.maturity: Two decades of independent confirmation across many groups and platforms; the interpretation is fully stable. Timing is delicate because the 2025 prize recognised neighbouring superconducting-circuit physics, so the committee may prefer to wait, but the maturity itself is not in doubt.
uncertainties: Proximity to the 2025 award (macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits) may make recognition feel repetitive.
Credit among the Yale, Chalmers/ETH and Sherbrooke contributors is not cleanly separable within three names.
My professional closeness to this field could bias my weighting.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 1995 proposal for quantum gates with trapped ions and the later neutral-atom and Rydberg schemes supplied the first concrete, physically complete blueprints for quantum computation and simulation. Foundational and lasting, with strong theory-experiment reach.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller are the clear joint originators of the trapped-ion gate and the broader programme; a two-person prize is a clean configuration and does not need a third name. Experimental realisation is largely credited to others (Wineland, Blatt and colleagues), already partly honoured in 2012.
assessment.maturity: Thirty years of experimental realisation and independent validation; very mature and arguably overdue. Impact is established beyond ion traps.
uncertainties: Zoller also appears on other entries, so the overlap between a lattice-simulation and a quantum-computing recognition has to be handled.
Whether the committee views this as theory that follows 2012 or as a separate discovery is not settled by the supplied text.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The magic-wavelength optical lattice clock removed the Doppler and recoil limits and brought fractional uncertainties to the 1e-18 level, enabling redefinition of the second, geodesy and tests of fundamental physics. Very clear and measurable impact.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength scheme; Ye led the strontium-lattice demonstrations and the record-precision development. A two-name allocation is natural, though Hall and Hansch were honoured in 2005 for the comb and others (Ludlow, Hinkley, Ushijima) contributed to performance.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature, with multiple independent labs reproducing the results and international metrology adopting it; timing is appropriate.
uncertainties: The boundary with ion clocks and comb-related recognition (2005, 2012) may reduce perceived novelty.
I have not independently checked every uncertainty record claimed for the best clocks.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realised the Hubbard model with tunable parameters, including the superfluid-Mott transition and single-site-resolved microscopy, giving a platform for quantum simulation of strongly correlated matter. Broad and durable.
assessment.attribution: The Jaksch-Zoller proposal and the Greiner-Bloch Mott-insulator experiment are decisive; Esslinger's fermionic work and the microscope groups are also central, so the four-name list forces a hard choice. I propose Bloch, Greiner and Zoller as the most defensible core, with unresolved competing claims.
assessment.maturity: Mature for the lattice experiments; quantum-simulation advantage on genuinely hard problems is still being established, so some of the promise is not yet fully realised.
uncertainties: Esslinger, Jaksch, Hänsch (earlier groundwork) and the microscope pioneers have credible claims.
Overlap with B044 and B039 through Zoller.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum spin Hall effect and topological insulators, with the quantum anomalous Hall effect, opened a major branch of condensed matter physics built on topological band invariants and protected edge transport. Original and conceptually clean.
assessment.attribution: Kane (with Mele) supplied the theory; Molenkamp's HgTe experiment confirmed the prediction; Xue's group realised the quantum anomalous Hall effect. Mele and Bernevig/Zhang are important theory contributors not covered by this exact credit list, and the combination spans two related effects.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent experimental confirmation; the field is mature, though 2016 already honoured topological phases, which weakens the sense of novelty.
uncertainties: The compound discovery (QSH versus QAH) may need distinct recognition.
Theory credit (Mele, Zhang) is complicated and the 2016 prize overlap is real.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: IceCube's observation of a diffuse flux of astrophysical neutrinos and the TXS 0506+056 and Galactic-plane results opened neutrino astronomy at TeV-PeV energies. A major instrumental and scientific achievement.
assessment.attribution: Halzen led the concept and the collaboration science; Karle and Spiering made key construction and collaboration contributions. Large-collaboration credit is difficult to compress and AMANDA/Baikal precursors matter.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed over a decade and with later multi-messenger results; some source identifications are still emerging, so the picture is incomplete but the discovery itself is secure.
uncertainties: Source associations are not fully settled.
Fair credit among IceCube founders and precursor experiments is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum cryptography proposed information-theoretically secure key exchange based on quantum mechanics, a conceptually deep link between foundations and information, now deployed commercially and over satellites.
assessment.attribution: BB84 by Bennett and Brassard is the decisive origin; Ekert's entanglement-based protocol is an independent, closely related proposal. Wiesner's earlier conjugate-coding idea complicates priority and is outside the credited set.
assessment.maturity: Protocols are well understood and demonstrated; practical security against device imperfections remains an active matter. The 2022 prize partly neighbours this subject.
uncertainties: Wiesner's priority claim cannot be accommodated by the exact names.
Overlap with the 2022 prize on entanglement and quantum information.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological and surface-code error correction gave a route to fault tolerance with realistic local operations and thresholds, which is the central requirement for large quantum processors. Conceptually deep and increasingly experimentally relevant.
assessment.attribution: Kitaev's toric code and anyon-based ideas are the core; Bravyi (with Kitaev) and Preskill (with Dennis, Kitaev, Landahl) contributed fault-tolerance analysis. Dennis, Landahl and Fowler are not credited and a prize would be hard to allocate.
assessment.maturity: Recent below-threshold experiments are encouraging but fault-tolerant computation has not been demonstrated at scale; likely premature relative to the other entries.
uncertainties: Attribution among Kitaev, Bravyi, Preskill and coauthors is contested.
